thesis.what_must_be_true: The AI-driven leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM and advanced-packaging capex cycle must remain intact through at least FY2028, with AMAT holding share in Semiconductor Systems and converting record revenue into expanding operating margins and positive free cash flow after the current inventory build; if equipment demand or memory customer capex rolls over, the multi-year growth thesis and my margin path break.

validated.preview_note: Applied Materials reports fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended July 26) in late August. The setup is bullish: Q2 printed record revenue of $7.91B and management raised its calendar-2026 semicap growth outlook to >30%, citing AI infrastructure build-out across logic, DRAM/HBM and advanced packaging. It guided Q3 to $8.95B +/-$500 and non-GAAP EPS $3.36 +/-$0.20. We forecast revenue of $8.95B (midpoint) but non-GAAP EPS of ~$3.45 - a modest beat - on operating margins near 33.8% as mix stays weighted to high-margin Semiconductor Systems. The three factors that matter: (1) magnitude and mix of AI-led orders, especially foundry/logic and HBM; (2) gross-margin trajectory given the flagged inventory/logistics build; (3) the strategic-investment mark-to-market swing that pushed GAAP above non-GAAP in Q2. Reaction hinges on Q4 guidance: we expect ~$9.3B +/-$500 and non-GAAP EPS ~$3.45 +/-$0.20. Downside risks are China exposure, any HBM/DRAM capex push-out, and a working-capital-driven FCF dip (we model Q3 FCF ~$115M).
validated.reasoning: Anchors from the Q2 FY26 10-Q/8-K (accession 0001628280-26-035071): revenue $7,910M, GAAP EPS $3.51, non-GAAP EPS $2.86, and Q3 guidance of $8,950M +/-$500 / non-GAAP EPS $3.36 +/-$0.20. I anchor Q3 revenue at the guidance midpoint ($8.95B) but expect a slight non-GAAP beat to ~$3.45 because AMAT has beaten the non-GAAP guide in recent quarters and operating leverage is favorable. Gross margin ~50.1% (above Q2's 50.0% non-GAAP) on Semiconductor Systems mix; operating margin ~33.8%. Other income, net of ~$815M embeds a ~$690M strategic-investment gain similar to Q2, which is why GAAP EPS ($4.09) sits above non-GAAP ($3.45) - consistent with the Q2 print where non-GAAP was $520M below GAAP. The bridge removes that gain and adds back acquisition/tax items to arrive at non-GAAP NI of $2,753M (EPS $3.45). Cash flow: CFO ~$765M, pressured by a larger working-capital build (inventory/logistics for AI); capex ~$650M; FCF ~$115M. Buybacks $400M, dividends $365M. Balance sheet rolls forward with cash falling to ~$5.4B. Quarterly path and FY horizons extend AI-driven growth: revenue compounding low-double-digits through FY2029, operating margins holding ~33-34%, FCF turning sustainably positive as the inventory build normalizes. Key swing factor is the strategic-investment gain magnitude and HBM/logic capex timing.
